author: Bobby Grayson
description: 1) A struct-shaped state is flattened, so no value of that struct type ever exists in the model; binding one (s2 = %(state | f: v) then returning s2) is refused with a clear message. The state must be returned directly, or its fields bound. 2) hd/1 raises on the BEAM but an expression here cannot, so it renders as List.headD at the element type's default; an element type with no default (a tagged union) is an error that asks you to match on the list instead. 3) A capture is one-argument only (&1); &2 has nothing to refer to. 4) x1 is reserved as the binder of a capture. 5) Enum.map's result element type is inferred from the lambda body when possible, otherwise an expected type is needed. 6) A statement with an effect (a send, a spawn) before an if/case body is refused: it would have to be pushed into every branch. 7) An .exs driver cannot use struct literals, because a script is expanded before Code.require_file has run; struct/2 is the workaround, and elixir/ringlog.exs says so. 8) Declarations must be emitted in dependency order (a struct used by a tagged union first): Lean has no forward references. 9) A whole-state part the right-hand side never mentions must be renamed _part or Lean's unused-variable linter warns.
title: Translator limits and rules found by the log store shape
